classification: Source inspiration / credited photographic aperture recreation
credit: Julián Leiss / Ajedrez Film Poem; underlying archival film authors and reuse rights remain unverified.

source.audio: Present in original; unreviewed and deliberately omitted from derivative.

derivative.role: Individual moving photographic aperture only, without the source film typography or whole portrait frame.
derivative.runtimeBinding: Genuine HTTP201 upload268, exact derived bytes and source lineage retained in the official external receipt. No source/native Framer binding is claimed by this provenance.

nativeBinding.sourceHierarchy: Existing ordinary aperture Frame under film-phase-29, beneath the same Film Context. No native child nodes exist inside this aperture; its source image fill remains the poster.
nativeBinding.preserve: Native IDs/parents/geometry and image fill; all outside typography, rules and editable phase contents.

playback.fit: The 49 source frames are fitted to the existing two-second native phase; adjacent cuts are unchanged and remain approximate.
playback.clock: The existing same-module Film Context is the only timeline. Pause/replay/offscreen/document-hidden/reduced/frozen states control admission; no independent media clock drives the film.
playback.decoder: One live client uses the existing monarchic.source-portfolio-media.v1 gate and the shared two-decoder cap. An actual preexisting H4 gate is exercised by focused browser checks.
playback.surface: One 480×510 2D canvas supplies only photographic pixels. It retains the last decoded image on pause and is hidden for Canvas/export/reduced targets; native fill supplies the static poster.

localEvidence.scope: Actual local decoded source pixels and native-like React Frame child forwarding; actual Framer compilation/paint/persistence still require the retained-aperture probe.

remaining: Final locked Nix and actual Framer native Frame child-forwarding/clock/decoder/moving-paint/Phone proof remain required. Other photo-strip choreography, film audio and exact cuts are not restored by this single aperture.
